title: The Coset Structure of Non-Commuting Cliques
body: The key structural theorem: if g and h are in a clique (gh ≠ hg), they must lie in different cosets of Z(G). If they were in the same coset, g⁻¹h would be central, and g and h would commute — contradicting the clique property. This gives the injection bound ω(Γ(G)) ≤ [G:Z(G)].

title: ω = 0 Characterizes Abelianness
body: The non-commuting graph has no edges (empty clique) precisely when every pair of elements commutes — i.e., when G is abelian. This is a clean biconditional that captures the zeroth level of the clique-number hierarchy.
